description: Social Studies matriculation 2019: topic → subtopic → concept/keywords index mapped to question ids and textbook pages. Used by the offline search tutor.

topics.title: Geography, the Earth and the Sun
topics.unit: G9 Units 1–2 – Subject Matter of Geography; Earth–Sun Relation
topics.concept: Branches of geography, latitude and longitude, local time, and the effects of the earth's rotation and revolution.

subtopics.title: Branches of geography
subtopics.concept: Regional geography studies all aspects (physical and human) of one region. Topical/systematic geography studies one theme (e.g. climate, population) across many places. Physical and human geography are the two main systematic branches.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 1 – The Subject Matter of Geography

subtopics.title: Latitude, longitude and time
subtopics.concept: Latitudes run east–west and measure position north/south of the equator (0°, the longest line and a great circle). Meridians run north–south, meet at the poles and measure position east/west of the prime meridian (0°, through Greenwich near London). 15° of longitude = 1 hour; places to the east are ahead in time.

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.2 Effects of the Earth's rotation – differences in local time
3.3 Factors that influence temperature – latitude (the equator)

subtopics.title: Rotation, revolution and seasons
subtopics.concept: Rotation causes day and night, the apparent movement of the sun, differences in local time, deflection of winds (Coriolis) and tides. Revolution plus the 23½° tilt causes the seasons and changing day length. June solstice: sun overhead at the Tropic of Cancer, NH summer / SH winter. Seasons in latitudinal zones depend on the shifting overhead sun (equatorial zone 0°–5°: one season).

textbook_refs.section: 2.3 Revolution of the Earth – seasons and insolation

topics.title: Weather and climate
topics.unit: G9 Unit 3 – Weather and Climate; G10 Unit 1 – World Climates
topics.concept: Atmosphere, temperature, pressure, winds, precipitation and the major world climate types.

subtopics.title: Atmosphere and elements of weather
subtopics.concept: Elements: temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, precipitation (latitude is a control, not an element). Troposphere = lowest layer (10–16 km) where weather happens. Lapse rate 6.5 °C per 1000 m. Daily mean = (max + min) ÷ 2; range = max − min. Frost = ice crystals formed near the ground below freezing point.

subtopics.title: Winds and wind belts
subtopics.concept: Coriolis effect: winds deflect right in the NH and left in the SH, so winds blowing towards the equator turn west (trade winds, polar easterlies). Monsoons are seasonal winds that reverse between summer (sea → land, wet) and winter (land → sea, dry).

textbook_refs.section: 2.2 Effects of Rotation – land and sea breezes

subtopics.title: Major types of world climate
subtopics.concept: Tropical wet (0°–5°): hot, wet, broad-leaved evergreen rainforest with tall hardwoods and a dense canopy. Tropical monsoon 5°–15°. Other groups: dry, warm temperate, cool temperate, cold and highland climates.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 1 – Major Types of World Climates

topics.title: Landforms, tectonic forces and gradation
topics.concept: Internal (tectonic) forces build landforms; external (gradational) forces of rivers, wind and waves wear them down and deposit material.

subtopics.title: Plate tectonics and tectonic forces
subtopics.concept: Divergent boundaries form rift valleys and ridges; convergent boundaries form trenches (ocean–ocean), fold mountains and volcanoes (ocean–continent); transform boundaries form faults such as the San Andreas. Faulting, folding, volcanism and earthquakes are tectonic processes.

textbook_refs.section: 1.5.2 Distribution of earthquakes in the world

topics.title: Population, settlement and development
topics.concept: World population growth and structure, population problems, settlement types, development and resources, and human impact on the environment.

subtopics.title: Population growth and structure
subtopics.concept: Population grew slowly until the industrial revolution because of high infant mortality, short life expectancy, famines and undernourishment. An expansive pyramid has a broad base (high birth rate, young population). Demographic transition and migration.

textbook_refs.reference: UN World Population Prospects; general geography

subtopics.title: Population problems
subtopics.concept: Developing countries: rapid growth, unemployment, under-utilisation of resources, uneven distribution. Developed countries: aging population, small workforce, and urbanization problems (pollution, congestion, noise, crime).

textbook_refs.reference: UN World Population Prospects; general geography

subtopics.title: Human settlement
subtopics.concept: Components: shelter, infrastructure (roads, water, power) and services (education, health, culture, recreation). Rural settlement shapes: linear, rounded, star-shaped, T-shaped (minor road meets major road). Dispersed vs nucleated settlements.

subtopics.title: Development and resources
subtopics.concept: Malthus: population grows geometrically, food arithmetically. Enough food is produced – hunger is a distribution problem. South Africa is the industrialised exception in sub-Saharan Africa. Resource conservation: substitution (e.g. solar for oil), recycling (aged cars smelted and reused), preservation.

textbook_refs.section: 4.3 Resources and development – renewable and non-renewable resources

subtopics.title: Cultural impact on the environment
subtopics.concept: Population growth and modern technology modify the environment. Problems: deforestation, desertification, global warming (sea-level rise, droughts disrupting farming, ozone depletion), acid rain (a large volume of pollutants), air pollution.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 5 – The Representation of Relief on Maps
textbook_refs.section: 5.1 Representation of relief – natural and cultural features

topics.title: Regions and map work
topics.unit: G9 Units 4, 6; G10 Unit 5; G11 Unit 8
topics.concept: The concept of region, map scales, representation of relief and reading landforms on contour maps.

subtopics.title: Scales, relief representation and contour maps
subtopics.concept: RF 1:50,000 = 1 cm to 0.5 km. Relief methods: contours, spot heights, trigonometrical stations, bench marks (accurate), plus hachures, hill shading, form lines and physiographic diagrams. Contour interval = difference between neighbouring contours. Landforms: hill, ridge, spur (V points downhill), valley (V points upstream), saddle/col. Gradient = VI ÷ HE × 100 %. Inter-visibility is tested with a section.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 5 – The Representation of Relief on Maps
textbook_refs.section: 5.1 Representation of relief – natural and cultural features

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 6 – Scales and Classification of Map Scales
textbook_refs.section: 6.1 Classification of maps by scale – large scale maps

topics.title: Physical and human geography of Eritrea
topics.concept: Position, size, relief, geology, water, climate, vegetation, soils, economy and population of Eritrea.

subtopics.title: Position, size and relief of Eritrea
subtopics.concept: Eritrea is larger than Seychelles, Andorra and Malta. Relief: Eastern Lowlands (Djibouti border to Ras Kassar, below 500 m), Western Lowlands (Zobas Anseba and Gash-Barka, 500–1000 m), the Eastern Escarpment and the Highlands. The Central Plateau (flat, fertile, moderate climate) and Southern Plateau (flat, adequate rain, fertile black soils) are important for agriculture. Mountains lack level land and have thin soils.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea
textbook_refs.section: 7.2 Drainage systems – the western drainage (River Setit)

subtopics.title: Water resources of Eritrea
subtopics.concept: Surface water is unreliable for irrigation and hydro-power because of irregular rainfall and high evapo-transpiration, so small-scale development is recommended. Highlands: groundwater depleted by heavy pumping, and siltation of surface water. Lowlands: low recharge, salinity.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea
textbook_refs.section: 7.2 Drainage systems – the western drainage (River Setit)

subtopics.title: Natural vegetation and wildlife
subtopics.concept: Varied relief and climate give many habitats. Globally endangered: African wild ass (critically endangered) and Nubian ibex; nationally endangered: African elephant (Haikota, Augaro, Antore).

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 4 – Natural Vegetation and Wildlife in Eritrea
textbook_refs.section: 4.6.2 Present situation of wildlife in Eritrea

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 4 – Natural Vegetation and Wildlife in Eritrea

subtopics.title: Soils and soil conservation
subtopics.concept: Soil degradation causes: steep slopes, deforestation, overgrazing (plus drought and war). Conservation: terraces, afforestation, shelter belts (against wind erosion), check dams, area closures. Soil water depends on vegetation, climate and soil physical characteristics.

subtopics.title: Economic activities
subtopics.concept: Agriculture, fishing, mining, industry, trade, tourism. Road transport: Italian-built roads linking the ports with the hinterland (e.g. Mendefera–Areza, Dekemhare–Nefasit) and post-independence all-weather roads (Keren–Afabet, Dekemhare–Tserona).

topics.title: Ancient civilizations (Grade 9)
topics.concept: Concepts of history, human evolution, Mesopotamia and Egypt, India and China, Greece and Rome.

subtopics.title: India and China
subtopics.concept: Caste system: Brahmins (priests) → Kshatriyas (warriors) → Vaisyas (commoners) → Sudras → Untouchables. Hinduism: reincarnation; created a legacy of inequality. Buddhism: Four Noble Truths, meditation. Chinese philosophies: Confucianism (government open to men of wisdom and skill, not only noble birth), Taoism, Legalism (people evil by nature → strong ruler). Chinese inventions: magnetic compass, paper, printing, gunpowder.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 4 – China and India (3000 B.C.E.–500 C.E.)

subtopics.title: Greco-Roman civilization
subtopics.concept: Greek philosophers: Socrates, Plato (The Republic), Aristotle (three good governments: monarchy, aristocracy, constitutional government). Oligarchy = rule by the few. Rome preserved and transmitted Greek civilization.

textbook_refs.section: 5.1 Greek culture – works of history and drama

topics.title: Ancient and medieval Eritrea (Grade 9 Unit 6)
topics.unit: G9 Unit 6 – Ancient and Medieval Eritrea
topics.concept: Peoples of Eritrea, Aksum and its decline, medieval developments, Turkish rule, Tigrean expansion and Egyptian rivalry.

subtopics.title: Peoples and social organisation of Eritrea
subtopics.concept: Linguistic groups: Nilotic (Nara, Kunama), Cushitic (Hidareb, Bilen, Saho, Afar), Semitic (Tigrinya, Tigre, Rashaida). Nara and Kunama: egalitarian, common linguistic family, crop cultivation + animal husbandry, clan administration by a council of elders. Bilen: Bet Taqwe moved from Hamasien to the Keren area (16th–17th c.), where Bet Tarke had already settled.

textbook_refs.section: 6.3 Population movements – Northern Highlands, Sahel and Senhit

subtopics.title: Medieval Eritrea (7th–19th centuries)
subtopics.concept: Key developments: Beja expansion and peaceful spread of Islam; Agew immigration; Turkish (1557 Massawa/Hirghigo) and Portuguese attempts at conquest in the 16th century; population movements; Tigrean and Amhara feudal expansion (18th–19th c.) to collect tribute, reach the coast for arms and profit from Red Sea trade. Raesi Wubie tortured people with hot roasted peas poured into their ears. Egypt–Tigrai-Amhara rivalry in the 19th century.

textbook_refs.section: 6.4 Eritrea in the 19th century – the Egyptian threat (Gundet)
6.3 Population movements – Northern Highlands, Sahel and Senhit

topics.title: Medieval and early-modern world (Grade 10 Units 1–11)
topics.concept: Medieval Europe and Byzantium, Islam, the Americas, African kingdoms, Renaissance and Reformation, exploration and slave trade, scientific revolution.

subtopics.title: Medieval Europe, Byzantium and the Crusades
subtopics.concept: First European university: Bologna. Byzantine emperor appointed the Patriarch and controlled church and state; Greek official language; Eastern Orthodox Church. Crusades: weakened feudalism and nobles, strengthened kings → nation-states; revival of learning. Black Death (1347) = worst disaster of the Late Middle Ages.

subtopics.title: Rise and expansion of Islam
subtopics.concept: Islam is monotheistic and accepts earlier prophets. Mohammed was persecuted in Mecca and fled to Medina in 622 – the Hijrah. His successors were caliphs (Abu Bakr first). Rapid expansion: Byzantine and Persian empires weakened by war, their subjects dissatisfied, local people accepted Arab rule, a large army with brilliant generals, religious motivation, Arab migration.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 2 – The Rise of Islam, 600–1500 C.E.
textbook_refs.section: 2.1 The Arabs and the rise of Islam – the caliphs

subtopics.title: Civilizations of the Americas and Sub-Saharan Africa
subtopics.concept: Maya: 300–900 C.E., Yucatán, city-states, temples and calendar. Ghana (from c. 500 C.E.) → Mali (Sundiata, mid-13th c., Timbuktu) → Songhai. East Africa: Swahili (Bantu + Arabic). Central Africa: Luba, Lunda, Kongo. Bantu spread over sub-Saharan Africa over two millennia.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Civilizations in the Americas, 500–1500 C.E.

textbook_refs.section: 4.3 Central Africa – the Kingdom of Kongo

subtopics.title: Renaissance and Reformation
subtopics.concept: Renaissance: urban, recovery from the 14th-century disasters, emphasis on individual ability; Machiavelli, The Prince. Reformation causes: corruption in the Church, worldly Renaissance popes, sale of indulgences, church taxes to Rome; Luther's Ninety-five Theses (1517).

subtopics.title: European exploration and the slave trade
subtopics.concept: Portugal took the lead in exploration (Prince Henry); Diaz 1488, Columbus 1492, da Gama 1498. Slavery existed in Africa before the Europeans; Europeans first bought slaves from local African merchants; the trade grew with the discovery of the Americas; 12–15 million Africans taken; West Africa most affected.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 7 – European Exploration and the African Slave Trade 1500–1800
textbook_refs.section: 7.1 European exploration – Treaty of Tordesillas and the Spanish Empire

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 5 – Colonialism and Independence Movements in Latin America

subtopics.title: Scientific Revolution
subtopics.concept: Copernicus (1543) put the sun, not the earth, at the centre (heliocentric); Galileo, Kepler and Newton followed.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 11 – The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment

topics.title: Italian colonialism in Eritrea (Grade 10 Unit 12)
topics.unit: G10 Unit 12 – Italian Colonization in Eritrea
topics.concept: Italian expansion, colonial policy phases, administration, resistance.

subtopics.title: Italian expansion, policies and administration
subtopics.concept: Expansion helped by the Great Famine 1888–92, harsh Italian measures, and people tired of Tigrean/Egyptian raids. First phase (1890–96): settler colony, land alienation. Aims: settle poor Italian farmers; raw materials and market; springboard for expansion into Ethiopia. Justice: Italian penal code for all; civil code where one party was Italian; Sharia/customary law for Eritrean civil cases. Nakura island prison.

textbook_refs.section: 12.1 Italian expansion – Treaty of Wuchale and the Mereb-Belesa-Muna line

subtopics.title: Eritrean resistance to Italian rule
subtopics.concept: Degiat Aberra (Abera) Hailu killed Captain Pettini at Walta Medhanit (c. 1891); Bahta Hagos's revolt – wounded and died at Halay, December 1894; Abubaker Ahmed (Saho) led Saho and Tigrigna fighters (1901); Mohammed Nurri (Saho) planned to enter Asmara and kill Governor Ferdinando Martini (1902).

textbook_refs.section: 12.1 Italian expansion – Treaty of Wuchale and the Mereb-Belesa-Muna line

topics.title: Revolutions, nationalism, imperialism and world wars (Grade 11 Units 1–10)
topics.concept: American and French revolutions, industrialization, unification, imperialism, WWI, interwar, WWII.

subtopics.title: American and French revolutions
subtopics.concept: George Washington commanded the Continental Army and became the first US president. French Revolution sequence: Estates-General (May 1789) → National Assembly → Bastille (14 July 1789) → Terror ends 1794 → Directory 1795 → Napoleon emperor 1804. The Third Estate = peasants, workers and the bourgeoisie (merchants, lawyers, doctors…).

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 The Old Regime – the three estates

subtopics.title: Industrialization, socialism and unification
subtopics.concept: Marx: history is the history of class struggle; bourgeoisie vs proletariat; proletariat would win; the state would wither away. Italian unification: Mazzini, Cavour, Garibaldi, Victor Emmanuel II (Bismarck unified Germany). Einstein: theory of relativity (1905).

textbook_refs.section: 3.3 Unification of Italy and Germany – Otto von Bismarck

subtopics.title: Colonialism in Asia, Latin America and Africa
subtopics.concept: Thailand (Siam) remained the only free state of Southeast Asia; the Philippines became a US colony (1898). Haiti (1804) was the first independent state in Latin America.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 5 – Colonialism and Independence Movements in Latin America
textbook_refs.section: 5.2 Independence movements in Latin America – Haiti

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 7 – European Exploration and the African Slave Trade 1500–1800
textbook_refs.section: 7.1 European exploration – Treaty of Tordesillas and the Spanish Empire

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 5 – Colonialism and Independence Movements in Latin America

subtopics.title: Nationalist movements around the world (Grade 11 Unit 9)
subtopics.concept: Middle East mandates after WWI: Iraq, Palestine and Jordan under Britain; Syria and Lebanon under France. Pan-Africanism (W.E.B. Du Bois, Marcus Garvey); Negritude stressed the uniqueness and importance of African culture and history (Léopold Senghor, Aimé Césaire). China: Mao Zedong's Communists escaped Chiang Kai-shek on the Long March (1934–35, about 9,600 km).

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 9 – Nationalisms and National Movements around the World
textbook_refs.section: 9.3 Nationalism in the Middle East – Zionism and Palestine

subtopics.title: World War I, interwar period and World War II
subtopics.concept: Central Powers: Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Turkey, Bulgaria (Russia was an Ally). Wilson's Fourteen Points: end secret treaties, free seas, arms reduction, League of Nations, national self-determination (reparations came from the Treaty of Versailles). WWII began 1 Sept 1939 (Poland); USA entered after Pearl Harbor (7 Dec 1941).

textbook_refs.section: 10.1 Causes of World War II – aggression of the dictators
7.2 The course of World War I – the two camps

topics.title: Eritrea under the British and the Federation (Grade 11 Units 11–12)
topics.concept: End of Italian rule, BMA, political parties, the Four Powers and the UN, federation and annexation.

subtopics.title: British period and political parties (1941–1952)
subtopics.concept: Keren fell 27 March 1941, Asmara 1 April 1941 – end of Italian rule. Mahber Fiqri Hager founded 5 May 1941 (president Gebremeskel Woldu, vice-president Abdulkadir Kebire, secretary Haregot Abbay). Pro-independence leaders: Ibrahim Sultan, Woldeab Woldemariam, Abdulkadir Kebire; Tedla Bairu led the Unionists. Four Great Powers: USA, Britain, France, USSR.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 11 – Eritrea during the British Period
textbook_refs.section: 11.3 Political parties – Al Rabita Al Islamiya

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 11 – Eritrea during the British Period
textbook_refs.section: 11.5 The UN and the Eritrean case – federal resolution

subtopics.title: The Federation (1952–1962)
subtopics.concept: Ethiopia violated the federation. Its economic policy aimed to weaken the Eritrean economy and to weaken the labour movement and force skilled Eritreans to migrate to Ethiopia.

textbook_refs.section: 12.1 The Eritrean government under the Federation

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 11 – Eritrea during the British Period
textbook_refs.section: 11.5 The UN and the Eritrean case – federal resolution

topics.title: The world since 1945 (Grade 12 Units 1–4)
topics.concept: Cold War, Asia and the Middle East since 1945, decolonization and independent Africa.

subtopics.title: The Cold War
subtopics.concept: NATO April 1949 (no Austria); Warsaw Pact 1955 (Soviet-led military alliance; Yugoslavia and Austria were not members). Sputnik I (1957) was the first man-made satellite. Berlin Wall (1961) = symbol of division. Bay of Pigs (1961) failed. Soviets crushed the Prague Spring in Czechoslovakia (1968). Gorbachev: perestroika. Former Yugoslavia: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Macedonia, Serbia, Montenegro. Non-Aligned Movement grew out of Bandung (1955).

subtopics.title: Asia and the Middle East since 1945
subtopics.concept: Israel proclaimed 14 May 1948; Knesset = parliament. PLO 1964; Six-Day War 1967; Camp David Accords 1978. Intifada = Palestinian uprising. China: Deng Xiaoping's Four Modernizations. Nasser angered the West (support for Kenya/Algeria, Czech arms deal, Bandung/NAM, recognition of PR China).

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 The Middle East – Camp David Accords
2.2 People's Republic of China – civil war
2.2.1 People's Republic of China – China after Mao

subtopics.title: Decolonization and Africa since independence
subtopics.concept: Algeria fought a bloody war against France (independent 1962); Guinea chose full independence in 1958 under Sékou Touré. Tanzania's Ujamaa villages (Nyerere). Steve Biko's Black Consciousness aimed to restore black self-respect. Cold War aid: Soviet support to Ethiopia (Derg), Angola (MPLA), Mozambique, Somalia (until 1977).

textbook_refs.section: 3.4 Decolonization in Belgian colonies – Rwanda and Burundi
4.1 Africa since independence – problems of nation building

topics.title: Eritrean armed struggle (Grade 12 Unit 5)
topics.concept: ELM, ELF, zonal commands, Adobha, EPLF, strategic offensive, independence.

subtopics.title: ELM, ELF and the zonal commands
subtopics.concept: ELM founded November 1958 in Port Sudan (Mahber Showate). ELF founded in Cairo (1960), chairman Idris Mohammed Adem. ELF attacked the ELM at Ela Tsaeda (1965). Zonal commands (1965) copied from the Algerian Revolution. Adobha Conference (August 1969): national congress within one year, preparatory committee, committee to investigate misdeeds.

textbook_refs.section: 5.1 The ELF – origin and the start of the armed struggle
5.5 First Organizational Congress of the EPLF

textbook_refs.reference: Standard histories of the Eritrean struggle (e.g. R. Iyob, The Eritrean Struggle for Independence, 1995)

subtopics.title: EPLF, strategic offensive and independence
subtopics.concept: EPLF Second (Organizational and Unity) Congress 1987; Nadew Command destroyed March 1988 (Afabet); Operation Fenkil liberated Massawa (February 1990); liberation 24 May 1991; referendum 23–25 April 1993 (99.8 % yes); independence proclaimed 24 May 1993.

textbook_refs.section: 5.1 The ELF – origin and the start of the armed struggle
5.5 First Organizational Congress of the EPLF

topics.title: Economics (Business & Economics Grades 10–12)
topics.unit: B&E G10 Units 1–2; G11 Unit 1; G12 Unit 1
topics.concept: Scarcity and economic systems, sectors, money and banking, demand and markets, national income, public finance and international trade.

subtopics.title: Scarcity, economic systems and sectors
subtopics.concept: Resources are limited but human wants are unlimited, so every society must choose (scarcity → choice → opportunity cost). Economic systems: traditional, command, free-market and mixed – in the real world most economies are mixed. Sectors: primary (farming, mining, quarrying, fishing), secondary (manufacturing – converting raw materials into goods, e.g. shoe making), tertiary (services such as transport, banking).

textbook_refs.section: 1.1 Scarcity and choice – basic economic questions

textbook_refs.reference: Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776)

subtopics.title: Money and financial institutions
subtopics.concept: Barter needs a double coincidence of wants; money removes it. Functions of money: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, standard of deferred payment. The central bank (Bank of Eritrea) issues the currency (Nakfa), is banker to the government and controls commercial banks (Commercial Bank of Eritrea, Housing and Commerce Bank …).

textbook_refs.section: 2.1.1 Functions of money – unit of account
2.3 Central bank – functions of the Bank of Eritrea
2.2 Value of money – inflation and deflation
2.1.1 Functions of money – store of value (liquidity)

subtopics.title: Demand, revenue and market structures
subtopics.concept: Law of demand: price and quantity demanded are inversely related, other things being equal (ceteris paribus). Substitutes are used in place of each other (honey/sugar); complements are used together (car and gasoline). Total revenue = price × quantity; average revenue = TR ÷ Q; marginal revenue = extra revenue from one more unit. Market structures: perfect competition, monopolistic competition, oligopoly, monopoly (single seller), monopsony (single buyer).

textbook_refs.section: 1.2 Determinants of demand – price of related goods

subtopics.title: National income, investment and public finance
subtopics.concept: Circular flow: households receive factor incomes – rent (land), wages (labour), interest (capital), profit (entrepreneurship). Investment = spending on new capital goods (machinery, tractors, buildings). Economic growth = a sustained increase in national income/output. Taxes are the single biggest source of government revenue.

textbook_refs.reference: IMF World Economic Outlook database (GDP, current prices)

textbook_refs.section: 1.1 Macroeconomics – aggregate variables (growth, employment, price level)

subtopics.title: Balance of payments and exchange rates
subtopics.concept: Trade surplus: exports exceed imports; deficit: imports exceed exports. The exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another. More foreign tourists → more demand for Nakfa (supply of foreign currency rises) → the Nakfa appreciates against that currency.

textbook_refs.reference: World Trade Organization – 'What is the WTO?' (wto.org)
Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776)

topics.title: Accounting (Business & Economics Grades 10–12)
topics.unit: B&E G10 Unit 3; G11 Unit 2; G12 Unit 2
topics.concept: Purpose and users of accounting, business types, the accounting equation, financial statements, cash control and plant/intangible assets.

subtopics.title: Purpose and users of accounting; types of business
subtopics.concept: Accounting records and reports an organisation's economic activities. Users: owners/investors, bankers and suppliers (creditors), government (taxes), managers, employees. Service businesses sell services; merchandising businesses buy goods produced by others and resell them; manufacturing businesses make products. Forms of ownership: sole proprietorship (one owner), partnership, corporation.

subtopics.title: Accounting equation and financial statements
subtopics.concept: Assets = Liabilities + Capital (owner's equity). Assets are resources owned (cash, land, machinery, prepaid rent); liabilities are debts owed; capital is the owner's claim (not an asset). Current assets are converted to cash within one year. The balance sheet (statement of financial position) shows assets, liabilities and capital on a given date, normally at the end of each fiscal period (usually a year); the income statement shows revenues and expenses for a period – revenue > expenses = net income.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Bookkeeping for a Service Business
Unit 3 – Bookkeeping for a Service Business
Unit 3 – Bookkeeping for a Service Business

subtopics.title: Cash control, interest and plant/intangible assets
subtopics.concept: Good internal control: pay by pre-numbered cheque signed by an authorised person after reviewing the approved invoice; the bank gives an independent record. Interest is the cost of using (borrowing) someone else's money. Intangible assets are long-term legal rights without physical substance: patents, copyrights, trademarks, franchises, goodwill (prepaid expenses and receivables are current assets, not intangibles).

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 2 – Control of Cash, the Payroll and Payroll Records, and Plant Assets

topics.title: World regional geography (places and features)
topics.concept: Location facts that ESSCE Social Studies asks directly: continents, countries, deserts, lakes, straits, canals and cities of the world.

subtopics.title: Countries, deserts, lakes, rivers, straits and cities
subtopics.concept: Deserts: Sahara, Kalahari and Namib (Africa), Arabian, Thar, Atacama. Africa's largest lake is Victoria (≈68,800 km²). Khartoum lies at the confluence of the Blue and White Nile. The Strait of Gibraltar joins the Mediterranean to the Atlantic; the Suez Canal joins it to the Red Sea; Bab el Mandeb joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. Libya lies between Egypt and Algeria. Island states such as Seychelles lie wholly south of the equator.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 1 – Major Types of World Climates

textbook_refs.reference: World atlas / physical geography of Africa

topics.title: Economics – production costs, transport and economic policy (Business & Economics Grades 10–12)
topics.unit: B&E G10 Unit 1; G11 Unit 1; G12 Unit 1
topics.concept: Short-run costs, modes of transport, macroeconomic goals and inflation, and world economic organisations.

subtopics.title: Costs of production
subtopics.concept: Fixed costs (land, buildings, machines, rent, insurance) do not change with output and must be paid even when output is zero; variable costs (raw materials, wages of casual labour, fuel) change with output. Total cost = fixed + variable; average cost = TC ÷ Q; marginal cost = extra cost of one more unit.

subtopics.title: Modes of transport
subtopics.concept: Road: flexible, door-to-door, best for short distances. Railway: heavy and bulky goods over long distances. Water (sea): the cheapest way to carry bulky, non-perishable goods (containers) over long distances. Air: fastest but most expensive – used for perishable (flowers, vegetables) or precious (gold) goods.

subtopics.title: Economic policy goals, inflation and world economic organisations
subtopics.concept: Goals of economic policy: economic growth, employment creation (full employment), price stability, improving living standards and a fair distribution of income. Inflation = a sustained general rise in the price level; deflation = a general fall; stagflation = inflation with stagnant output and high unemployment. The WTO supervises trade agreements among member nations; the IMF and World Bank deal with finance and development.

subtopics.title: Business transactions, debit and credit
subtopics.concept: Only events that change assets, liabilities or capital in money terms are recorded (investment, payments, drawings, purchases on credit); hiring or firing an employee is not a transaction until money changes hands. Debit = left side of an account, credit = right side. Cash is the most liquid asset.

subtopics.title: Payroll: gross pay and net pay
subtopics.concept: Gross pay = total earnings before deductions. Net pay = gross pay − deductions (employee income tax and other withholdings such as pension or union dues). The employer withholds the income tax (Proclamation 62/1994) and pays the employee the net amount.
